course_description:
This course allows students to undertake an internship and related work-integrated learning.

This course consists of an industry placement in the field of writing, editing, and publishing, or communication. Students will undertake 80-100 hours of work-integrated learning, "solve" a problem for their provider, present their workplace ideas and reflections to their peers, and write a reflective essay.

course_aims: To enable students to undertake and reflect on a work-integrated learning experience.

learning_outcomes.description: Critically and reflexively analyse workplace tasks and apply effective problem-solving in real-world contexts
Communicate workplace insights confidently and respond effectively to questions and feedback
Evaluate peers' work and develop feedback skills aligned with industry practice
Identify and reflect on learning gained through the internship and articulate how it can be applied to future professional contexts.

assessment_details.category: Essay/ Critique, Participation/ Student contribution, Placement
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Identify a problem in the workplace. Identify a problem or opportunity in the workplace where you are undertaking your internship. It could be a system that could be streamlined, a lack of documentation in some aspect of work flow, or an idea for software or equipment that would make things easier for management or employees. Write up a 700-800 word proposal. If a submission does not adhere to the specified word RANGE, the content of the submission must be assessed and the element of non-compliance marked through a separate criterion (rubric), and the assessment marked up to the specified word limit. Please refer to Blackboard for full instructions. The next part of this assessment includes conducting a Peer Review of 2 x peer case studies as instructed in Blackboard by the date of the in-person Assessment Workshop. Finally, attend the Assessment Workshop to respond, in-person, to peer feedback and questions. (Note, you're not being assessed on your in-person performance, only on the content of your case study). assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submit via TurnItIn Link and Review peer work through the same link via the PeerMark tab.
Assignment to be submitted electronically via Blackboard and using TurnItIn . Before submitting any assignments for this course you must ensure you have completed UQ's compulsory online Academic Integrity Tutorial.
When you successfully submit your assessment to TurnItIn you will see text confirming your submission is complete, before being redirected to your Assignment inbox. On this page you can:
View the name of the submitted file View date and time of the upload Resubmit your paper (if necessary) Download your submitted paper Download digital receipt.
If you cannot see your submission in your Assignment inbox you should regard your submission as unsuccessful. Students are responsible for retaining evidence of submission by the due date for all assessment items, in the required form (e.g. screenshot, email, photo, and an unaltered copy of submitted work).
If the submission was not successful:
Note the error message (preferably take a screenshot). Go to your assignment page and see if it is possible to submit again. If you cannot submit again email your course coordinator immediately with the assignment attached.
Please visit this webpage for further advice on how to submit your TurnItIn assignment .
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 7 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Up to 7 days extensions are only available for the Case Study submission. This assessment involves a learning sequence and the use of peer-feedback in order for students to meet the learning outcomes, aligned to professional practice (LO2 and LO3). The timeliness of the peer-feedback and review process is a critical component of the learning sequence. A 28 day extension disrupts this learning sequence, and means that engaging in professional peer review and feedback is limited, reducing the learning opportunity and preventing students from meeting the learning outcome(s). A maximum 7 day extension enables some inclusion while keeping the learning sequence and pedagogical peer-review process intact so that students can still meet the learning outcomes.
Due to the in-person workshop factor included in this assessment, please contact the course coordinator if you're unable to attend the workshop. If you miss the workshop, there will be one make up session offered in which you'll complete the Assessment Workshop one-on-one, in-person, with the course coordinator. It will take place immediately after the Week 11 Workshop at 11am.
Alternative Assessment
If you have a Student Action Plan (SAPD) that applies to the case study, please contact the course coordinator immediately. Otherwise, to be eligible for alternative assessment, students must contact the course coordinator by Week 5 with relevant documentation. If there is an unforeseeable change to a student's circumstances (eg illness) after that date, please contact the course coordinator as soon as possible with documentation.
The make-up workshop is only available to students who have a genuine, documented reason for missing the workshop. Reasons may include: sudden/serious illness that requires a lengthy absence; or another documented reason for a lengthy absence. Reasons are documented in the ECP. Please refer there.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.

policies_and_procedures: University policies and procedures apply to all aspects of student life. As a UQ student, you must comply with University-wide and program-specific requirements, including the: Student Code of Conduct Policy Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and Procedure Assessment Procedure Examinations Procedure Reasonable Adjustments for Students Policy and Procedure AI for Assessment Guide Recording of Teaching Policy and Procedure Learn more about UQ policies on my.UQ and the Policy and Procedure Library . You'll also need to be aware of the following policies and procedures while completing this course: Work Integrated Learning and Work Experience Policy Course guidelines Communication Expectations While you are a student at UQ, all communication must be conducted according to the UQ Student Code of Conduct . The UQ Library has a helpful Communicate and collaborate online module . Email is the primary way for you to send messages to, and receive information from, the School and our staff. You must use your UQ email address (not a private address) to communicate with staff. You should add a clear subject line, including course code, and a 2-3 word statement. You can send email at any time, however, please do not expect responses outside normal working hours (Monday to Friday from ~8am to ~5pm). Emails that constitute bullying, harassment or discrimination against staff contravene the Student Code of Conduct. Emails like this will be reported to the University, and the matter will be pursued as misconduct. Learning activities
